title: Hedged requests and dynamic SLO enforcement for rerank endpoint
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: The rerank API is a critical latency-sensitive pathway for multiple Redwood customers. We observe tail latency spikes during regional congestion, transient GPU hiccups, and occasionally noisy model variants. Current defenses (simple timeouts and region fallback) are coarse, leading to either expensive global fallbacks or customer-facing errors.

Goal: Implement a layered reliability strategy centered on hedged requests (parallel speculative requests with controlled cancellation), quantile-driven dynamic SLO enforcement (adaptive timeouts set from live P95/P99 windows), and a lightweight quality-aware cheap-prefilter to avoid unnecessary hedging. Combined with a transparent circuit-breaker and probabilistic regional steering, this should reduce customer-facing errors, limit costly unnecessary fallbacks, and keep P95/P99 within SLOs while bounding cost impact.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end P95 latency for rerank endpoint improves by >=20% during simulated regional congestion compared to baseline without hedging
P99 latency and error rate do not regress by more than 10% versus baseline during normal traffic
Hedging cost overhead is limited to <=5% token cost increase at 99th percentile of production traffic patterns
Circuit breaker trips only when rolling window error rate > configured threshold and triggers documented fallback paths
New observability panels (per-region P50/P95/P99, hedging rate, hedged-success-rate, cost-impact) are available in Console and used in rollout checklist
Canary rollout plan completes with no customer-facing incidents and feature flags allow per-customer opt-out
implementation_plan:
1) Instrument: add metrics for per-request candidate latency, hedged-start, hedged-win, cancellation-latency, prefilter-score, and region-route-decision.

2) Prefilter: implement a cheap embedding similarity prefilter (CPU-bound, quantized embeddings) that runs in <5ms to decide if a request is eligible for hedging; false negatives are acceptable but false positives increase cost.

3) Dynamic SLO timeouts: compute adaptive timeouts per-model and per-region using a sliding 5m window of P95 and P99. Implement a percentile-smoothing function and minimum/maximum bounds. Expose knobs via runtime config.

4) Hedging layer: implement speculative duplicate requests to up to 2 alternate nodes/regions after the adaptive timeout with jitter and client-aware priorities. Ensure KV cache reuse where possible to avoid full recompute costs.

5) Circuit breaker: a sliding-window breaker that uses error-rate and latency-exceedance signals; when tripped, change routing to fallback cheap model variant or regional fallback based on policy.

6) Routing/steering: probabilistic regional steering using recent health scores; during congestion bias away from impacted region while keeping a small fraction of requests for health-check probing.

7) Testing & canary: unit tests, load tests with synthetic tails, chaos tests simulating regional packet loss and GPU OOMs; 1% canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with rollback thresholds.

8) Observability/dashboards/alerts: create dashboards and SLO alerts, plus playbook entries for operator response and cost anomaly detection.
risks:
- Hedging can increase cost if prefilter misses high-cost cases. Mitigation: conservative prefilter and hedging budget cap per-customer.
- Race conditions cancelling hedged requests could leave stranded compute on GPU nodes. Mitigation: best-effort cancellation plus short-lived hedges and server-side early-abort hooks.
- Adaptive timeouts may oscillate if windows are too short. Mitigation: smoothing and min/max bounds plus cooldown after rollout.
- Cross-region hedging increases egress and latency; mitigation: prefer local/secondary region and only use far regions when necessary.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for prefilter logic, adaptive timeout computation, and hedging cancellation.
- Integration test harness that replays recorded production traces and asserts cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Load test with injected tail latency: simulate 10% of nodes experiencing 3x latency for 15 minutes and measure P95/P99 with and without feature.
- Chaos test: simulate node OOMs and region packet loss and assert graceful degradation and successful fallbacks.
rollout_plan:
- Feature gated by org and model. Start with internal teams and a low-risk customer cohort.
- Canary stages: 1% traffic (24h) -> 5% (48h) -> 25% (72h) -> 100% (monitoring + manual approval between stages).
- Rollback criteria: sustained increase in P95/P99 > 15% for more than 30 minutes, or error-rate increase > 0.5% absolute.
observability_requirements: Create Console dashboards: per-region latency heatmap, hedging rate, hedged-success-rate, prefilter-pass-rate, cancellation-latency, hedging-cost-impact. Alerts: P95/P99 breach, hedging-rate above budget, circuit-breaker trips > 3 in 10 minutes. Add tracing spans to attribute latency to prefilter, main candidate, and hedged candidate.
outstanding_decisions:
- Exact hedging budget cap per-customer (suggest default 5% of requests or configurable token budget).
- Prefilter model: use CPU-quantized embedding index vs. lightweight neural classifier; default to embedding similarity for transparency.
- Whether to allow cross-region hedging by default or opt-in per-org due to egress concerns.
recent_updates: 2026-03-05: Spike completed for prefilter CPU prototype; median latency 3.8ms, 95th 7.2ms. Ava C.
2026-03-09: Dynamic timeout algorithm v1 implemented on staging; needs smoothing tuning. Marcus P.
2026-03-13: Load test with 15% node-level latency injection showed 22% P95 improvement with hedging+prefilter enabled. Observability panels ready for canary. Marcus P.
